status_summary: As of 2026-10-08 the 2024 Title IX rule is no longer in force and the regulatory text is back to its pre-2024 form. A federal court in Kentucky (Tennessee v. Cardona) vacated the 2024 rule in full on 2025-01-09 and a federal court in Texas (Carroll ISD) did the same on 2025-02-19; ED's later rule states that the appeals in both cases were dismissed in 2026, leaving the vacaturs final. ED's final rule titled Recodification of Title IX Rules (91 FR 61308, published and effective 2026-09-29) removes the 2024 amendments and restores 34 CFR part 106 to its text of 2024-04-28, which reflects the 2020 framework, with four omissions (a vacated cross-examination sentence, an obsolete appendix, an expired athletics adjustment period and expired review deadlines); ED issued it without notice and comment, citing the grants exemption and, alternatively, good cause. The rule does not itself define sex or address gender identity. Executive Order 14168 (signed 2025-01-20) defines sex as biological classification for the executive branch and directs agencies to rescind inconsistent guidance, including ED documents on Title IX issued between 2021 and 2024. On 2026-06-30 the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in West Virginia v. B.P.J., decided with Little v. Hecox, that Title IX allows schools to maintain sex-separated teams defined by biological sex and that the Idaho and West Virginia laws do not violate the Equal Protection Clause; as read through a summary of the opinion, the Court also stated that sex in Title IX can plausibly mean only biological sex. No Title IX regulation defining sex and no amendment of Title IX by Congress was located.

timeline.event: A federal court in Kentucky (Tennessee v. Cardona) vacates the 2024 Title IX rule in full (the rule had been published 2024-04-29 and took effect 2024-08-01); ED's 2026 recodification rule describes the vacatur as one of two final judgments, the other being Carroll ISD of 2025-02-19.

Executive Order 14168 is signed: it defines sex as an individual's biological classification (not including gender identity), directs agencies to apply the definition when interpreting federal law, and directs rescission of inconsistent agency guidance, including ED documents on Title IX issued between 2021 and 2024.
A federal court in Texas (Carroll ISD) vacates the 2024 Title IX rule in full, per ED's 2026 recodification rule.
Eleventh Circuit dismisses the last pending appeal over the 2024 rule (Alabama v. Cardona) as moot; defendants filed a voluntary dismissal on 2026-05-29.

The Supreme Court, 6-3 in West Virginia v. B.P.J. (No. 24-43) decided with Little v. Hecox (No. 24-38), holds that Title IX allows schools to maintain sex-separated sports teams defined by biological sex and that the West Virginia and Idaho laws do not violate the Equal Protection Clause; Justice Kavanaugh writes for the Court, and Justices Sotomayor, Kagan and Jackson dissent in part. As read through a summary, the opinion also says sex in Title IX can plausibly mean only biological sex.
